requested_by: lead ruling 2026-09-25: after T0 8/8 and before T3, vendor the news2 files into my own persistent tree; first establish whether `sources` pins paths as well as shas, and if it pins paths, name the path change in the T3 prereg and carry a one-cell bitwise comparison

question_1_does_sources_pin_paths.answer: YES -- the path is the dict KEY
question_1_does_sources_pin_paths.evidence: dlarch_train_f10.py:155  sources = {str(p): sha(p) for p in (...)}
question_1_does_sources_pin_paths.consequence: vendoring necessarily changes the sources signature; the resume guard (L260) and merge_folds (L105) both assert old['sources'] == sources, so a vendored run is by design not resumable from a /dev/shm-era fold

question_2_one_cell_bitwise_comparison.method: the SAME fold retrained with the vendored import paths, written to a throwaway root via the new --out-root flag, then compared to the delivered artifact. The delivered tree was READ ONLY throughout -- nothing was deleted, moved or restored.
question_2_one_cell_bitwise_comparison.conclusion: the path change is cosmetic for predictions

question_3_what_actually_changed.note: exactly one source sha differs, and it is the trainer I edited. The other six carry IDENTICAL shas across the two runs, which is the independent proof that the vendored copies are the same bytes as the /dev/shm originals -- separate from the vendor device's own read-back check.

what_was_vendored.code_files_7: the full IMPORT CLOSURE, not the 5 named in `sources`
what_was_vendored.closure_correction: my first attempt vendored only the 5 files `sources` names. That is a PROVENANCE list, not an import closure: T3 does `from book_universe import align, PATH, SHA` and the chain imports `combo_target`, neither of which appears in `sources`. Removing W/devices from sys.path with only those 5 vendored would have broken T3 at import time. The closure was enumerated by walking import statements transitively; book_universe and combo_target import only stdlib/numpy/scipy, so the walk terminates.

data_files_2_previously_pinned_NOWHERE.why_this_matters: both were read at the T3 branch (L214/L216) straight off /dev/shm and appeared in NO pinned list, so a change to either would have been SILENT. They are now vendored and asserted at the use site (BUNDLE_CFG_SHA / P1_MEMBERS_SHA). The pinned list and the read list are different lists; only comparing them shows the gap.

what_was_vendored.NOT_vendored_and_why: bulk data stays in /dev/shm: work/NEWS_FEATURES.npz 2,960,618,767 B (2.96 GB), work/legs.npz 35,418,454 B, receipts/P2B_FEATURES.json, receipts/P3_LEGS.json. 2.96 GB does not fit my /workspace quota (occupied 1.1 GB; last measured headroom ~1.6 GiB at 09:34Z; at 11:09:53Z I probed only to 512 MiB and stopped, because two lanes were writing and a quota-full write can fail silently). Those four ARE pinned via `inputs` and asserted per fold, so the residual exposure is AVAILABILITY (cost = a re-run), not correctness: a changed or missing W fails loudly and cannot silently train on other data.

residual_risk_named: if /dev/shm/news2_2026-09-23/work disappears before T3 finishes, T3 fails loudly and must be re-run after news2 rebuilds NEWS_FEATURES.npz. news2 has frozen the tree, verified 5/5 shas at 10:48:29Z, and committed to freeing their own pnoise work first. Whether to also vendor the 2.96 GB (needs ~3.1 GB of quota from the integrator) is lead's call, not mine -- I do not request resources on lead's behalf.
